secrets.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
secrets.optionalReason: Alternative AI backend; if neither OpenAI nor Anthropic key is set, app starts successfully in canned mode per README

secrets.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
secrets.optionalReason: Without it Cue runs in canned mode serving a real sample deck; users can also enter their own key per-request from the Settings UI

deployNotes: App reaches the database pod via db.pod:5432 using the DATABASE_URL environment variable

pgvector/pgvector:pg16 (docker-compose) is a Docker Hub namespaced image that fails on Nexlayer; use mirror.gcr.io/library/postgres:16-alpine and install pgvector extension via the server's schema.sql (CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector)
The Go binary applies server/schema.sql on every boot (NewStore), so no init script mount is needed on the db pod
The frontend is statically compiled into the Go binary (served from ./dist), so a single app pod serves both API and UI
The reference/ directory (deck engine templates) must be present in the image at runtime for compile.go to generate slides
Set ALLOW_ORIGIN to the external URL of the app pod or use * for development; CORS is enforced by the Go server

productionPlan.summary: Cue is a Go backend that serves both a compiled React frontend and an AI-powered deck generation API on port 8080, backed by PostgreSQL with pgvector for deck persistence. The Go binary embeds the built frontend from ./dist and the deck engine templates from ./reference — a single app pod handles everything. The one thing that matters most: the PostgreSQL password must never be a literal in the yaml, or the deploy will run with throwaway credentials that anyone can guess.

decisions.decision: Two pods: app (Go binary serving API + static frontend on 8080) and postgres (pgvector). No separate frontend pod needed because the Go binary serves the built Vite output from ./dist at runtime.
decisions.why: server/main.go registers both API routes and a static file handler for ./dist in the same Gin server, so one process serves everything.

decisions.decision: PostgreSQL with pgvector extension (pgvector/pgvector:pg16) in its own pod with a 10 Gi volume at /var/lib/postgresql. PGDATA is set to a subdirectory to survive the lost+found problem.
decisions.why: schema.sql runs CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector on every boot, which requires the pgvector binary to be present in the image; stock postgres:16-alpine does not include it.

decisions.decision: OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are intentionally left unset in the yaml — the app runs in canned mode (sample decks) and visitors supply their own keys per-request via X-User-OpenAI-Key header.
decisions.why: main.go selects a provider only when the key is non-empty; setting a placeholder would select OpenAI and then every generation fails. The BYOK path in handlers.go lets each visitor use their own key without any server-side secret.

decisions.decision: The existing multi-stage Dockerfile builds the frontend with node:22-alpine, the Go backend with golang:1.23-alpine, and produces a minimal alpine:3.20 runtime image. It patches the go.mod version typo and copies the reference/ engine directory for runtime template resolution.
decisions.why: compile.go's findEngineDir resolves deck templates from ./reference/engine at runtime — without it every slide generation fails the compile check.

decisions.decision: GET /api/health returns 200 with {ok: true, llm: '<provider name>'} — use this as the deployment readiness check.
decisions.why: main.go registers r.GET("/api/health", …) unconditionally; it confirms both HTTP serving and database connectivity (store is initialized before routes are registered).

fix_before_production.title: Replace literal Postgres password with ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
fix_before_production.why: The yaml currently has POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "cueai" and embeds cueai:cueai in DATABASE_URL — anyone with access to the deployment config gets database credentials. This is a secret exposure.

verify_after_deploy: GET /api/health on the app URL returns 200 with {"ok": true, "llm": "canned"}
GET / on the app URL returns 200 with the React landing page HTML
POST /api/decks with a test prompt and a valid X-User-OpenAI-Key header returns a deck JSON (confirms DB writes succeed and the pgvector extension loaded)
Restart the postgres pod and confirm GET /api/decks still returns previously created decks (confirms volume persistence)
open_questions: Should an OpenAI or Anthropic key be set server-side for a production demo, or is BYOK-only acceptable for the target users?

The pgvector image (pgvector/pgvector:pg16) is hosted on Docker Hub and may hit rate limits — confirm it pulls cleanly through the GCR mirror on first deploy, or switch to building a custom Postgres image with pgvector compiled in.
productionPlan.nexlayer_yaml:
application:
  name: cue-ai
  pods:
    - name: app
      image: "registry.nexlayer.io/YOUR_USER_ID/cue-ai-app:planned"
      path: /
      servicePorts:
        - 8080
      vars:
        PORT: "8080"
        HOSTNAME: "0.0.0.0"
        STATIC_DIR: "./dist"
        DATABASE_URL: "postgres://cueai:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@postgres.pod:5432/cueai?sslmode=disable"
        ALLOW_ORIGIN: "<% URL %>"
    - name: postgres
      image: "pgvector/pgvector:pg16"
      servicePorts:
        - 5432
      vars:
        POSTGRES_USER: "cueai"
        POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
        POSTGRES_DB: "cueai"
        PGDATA: "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata"
      volumes:
        - name: postgres-data
          size: 10Gi
          mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql
